sources.entry: python-slugify - A Python slugify library that translates unicode to ASCII.

summary.what_it_does: Generates slugs from str or UTF-8 bytes, lowercasing by default and replacing separators with a configurable delimiter (default '-'). In default ASCII mode it normalizes with NFKD and transliterates non-ASCII characters through a selected backend (text-unidecode, Unidecode, or AnyASCII). With allow_unicode=True it keeps Unicode word characters after NFKC normalization instead. It supports HTML entity and numeric reference decoding, max_length truncation with optional word-boundary and save_order handling, stopword removal, custom regex filtering, ordered find-and-replace rules, and a slugify command-line tool. Version 9.0.0+ adds an algorithm parameter: 'legacy' (default, frozen) or 'modern'.
use_cases: generate URL slugs from article titles
create ASCII-safe identifiers from non-English text
truncate slugs to a maximum length on word boundaries
how_to_run: python -m pip install 'python-slugify[unidecode]'  # optional Unidecode backend
python -m pip install 'python-slugify[anyascii]'  # optional AnyASCII backend
from slugify import slugify; slugify("C'est déjà l'été.")  # 'c-est-deja-l-ete'
notable: Explicit backend selection that raises ModuleNotFoundError instead of silently falling back
Frozen legacy algorithm kept for backward compatibility alongside an opt-in modern algorithm
Configurable replacement stages (pre, post, or both) with literal old/new rules and predefined German, Greek, and Cyrillic substitution lists
Keyword-only options added to the original positional API
caveats: Different backends produce different slugs for the same input, so pinning both the package and backend is recommended for stable identifiers
Slugs are not guaranteed unique, filesystem-safe, or safe as a full URL; the README says not to treat it as a security sanitizer
The README states that pull requests are generally not reviewed; it is issues-first, and changes to legacy output are not accepted
